title: Grammar Concepts  for Beginner Readers

title: Stories for Visualizing
description: When readers visualize a story, they draw pictures in their mind's eye, which are sparked by the text but anchored in their own knowledge. This is the same process that the illustrator of the story goes through when creating the images which accompany the story. This process increases our understanding and enjoyment of the text. These are stories we have found work well for this exercise (in English, Kannada and Hindi). Read these stories aloud, ask children to visualize the stories in their minds and then draw their representations on paper. You can also choose to focus on one particular page or aspect of each story. This exercise could be followed by looking at the illustrator's art-work on a projector and comparing them to illustrations drawn by the children. What is the same about the illustrations? What is different? Why do the children think this might be?

title: Read Aloud and Read Alone Stories
description: This is a list of titles which Chippersage has found most useful for additional reading practice. The criteria for selection included simplicity of text in terms of repetition of words and phrases, appealing illustrations to draw the reader in and culture specificity to ensure that the reader can relate to the text.

title: Animals
description: These stories can be used to highlight different aspects of the environment to children, including biodiversity, what humans can do differently and how to be more mindful of nature and creatures around us.

title: Language & Grammar
description: These books can be used to support English language development by demonstrating particular aspects of grammar. The stories can also help in reading practice and developing vocabulary. Specific learning outcomes are listed for each book.
